summary: Two explosions near the US consulate in Karachi, Pakistan, killed five and wounded more than fifty early Thursday, an attack Pakistani officials and a Forbes report speculated was timed to coincide with President George W. Bush's scheduled visit. Police said a suicide bomber apparently struck the vehicle of a United States diplomat and a second blast of unclear cause occurred minutes later in the Marriott Hotel parking lot about 60 feet from the consulate gate, and KUNA cited a hospital confirming at least five dead and over fifty injured, including a young Moroccan girl. The Associated Press said among the dead were a United States diplomat, a Pakistani consulate official, a consulate security guard and an unidentified woman; President Bush, speaking in New Delhi, said he would still visit Pakistan to meet President Musharraf, and AP noted the consulate had been targeted in 2002 (14 Pakistanis killed) and a 2004 time bomb was defused.
